title: What If the Milky Way Crashed Into Andromeda?

scenes.text: What if the Milky Way crashed into Andromeda? Almost none of the stars would actually collide.
Andromeda is racing toward us at about 250,000 miles an hour.
NASA's Hubble data predicts contact in roughly four billion years, and about two billion more to finish merging.
Stars are so far apart that they almost never hit each other. They just get flung into new orbits.
Our Sun would likely be thrown much farther from the galaxy's center, and NASA says Earth is in no danger from the crash.
The two spirals become one giant elliptical galaxy. Nothing hits you. The whole sky just gets rearranged.
